subject: Conversation buffering and intermittent token pause — mitigation steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Wong <rachel@novusai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Conversation buffering and intermittent token pause — mitigation steps

Hi Rachel / NovusAI team,

We’ve detected elevated buffering and intermittent pauses in streaming responses that impacted your live chat traffic on the r3.chat endpoint this morning. Scope: 08:42–09:05 PST, primarily traffic routed through us-west2 edge shards. Typical symptom: streaming token gaps of ~200–800ms every 4–12 tokens, visible as stuttering in your client.

First steps we recommend on your side (safe, non-disruptive):
- Switch to non-streaming (polling) for the next 20–40 minutes if your UX tolerates it.
- If you must stay on streaming, set client-side chunk timeout to 150ms and implement 500–1200ms jittered exponential backoff for reconnects.
- Temporarily reduce max_tokens to 512 for heavy-concurrency flows to lower tail token processing cost.
- Confirm your SDK keepalive and HTTP/2 window are set per our streaming best-practices (I’ll paste links below).

What we’re doing now:
- Triage is focused on an upstream batching heuristic that can introduce micro-pauses when sequence-length distribution shifts.
- We’ve isolated the affected edge shard pool and are preparing a controlled rollback of the heuristic.
- Collecting logs and a trace bundle; will attach a timeline and logs as soon as they’re packaged.

I’m copying Marissa and Ben from Customer Reliability (they’re on call) and will keep you updated with both mitigation and a short post-incident summary.

Attachments: incident_timeline_20270312.csv (summary timeline)

Thanks,
Irene Choi

Subject: Re: Conversation buffering and intermittent token pause — mitigation steps

Hi Rachel — short answers first: yes, it’s safe to keep traffic live if you switch the affected routes to polling for ~30 minutes; that avoids client-visible stuttering and prevents session drops in most cases.

What we’ve deployed so far (immediate mitigations):
- Rolled back the sequence-length batching heuristic on the us-west2 edge pool at 08:58 PST.
- Restarted two affected edge shards to flush in-memory batching windows (09:04 PST).
- Deployed a hotfix to the streaming keepalive/flush path to reduce micropause probability at the kernel level (09:18 PST).

Recommended customer-side actions (summary):
- Toggle to short polling for 30 minutes (non-streaming API calls every 300–800ms).
- Cap concurrency per client to 8 streams while we stabilize.
- Add 500–1200ms jittered backoff to reconnect logic.

Artifacts and links:
- Packed logs: packed-logs-usw2-20270312.tar.gz (attached) — contains edge shard traces and token timing samples.
- Incident timeline CSV: incident_timeline_20270312.csv (attached earlier).
- Support ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4581
- Logs/drill: https://drive.google.com/incident/novusai-20270312/logs

Short-term guidance if you prefer not to switch to polling: set stream_chunk_timeout=150ms and lower max_tokens to 512 for high-throughput flows. That reduces the chance of client-visible gaps while we complete stabilization.

I’ll follow up with a brief postmortem later today; Marissa will share the timeline and root cause once validated. Please ping me directly if you want a dedicated Zoom with our infra team — happy to run a joint triage.

Attachments: packed-logs-usw2-20270312.tar.gz, patch-rollback-notes.md

Thanks,
Irene
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Wong <rachel@novusai.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary: conversation buffering (us-west2) — root cause and next steps

Rachel — following up with the validated post-incident notes and recommended permanent changes. Thanks again for your patience this morning.

Timeline (validated):
- 08:40 PST: small increase in long-tail sequence-lengths from a NovusAI A/B experiment (higher avg tokens per request).
- 08:42 PST: elevated per-token gaps start to appear for a subset of us-west2 edge shards.
- 08:58 PST: we identified a regression in a batching-window heuristic that began to over-group requests when sequence-length variance increased.
- 09:04 PST: targeted restarts of two shards; 09:18 PST: hotfix to streaming flush path deployed; 09:25 PST: observed stabilization and end-user symptom reduction.

Root cause: a recent change to continuous-batching window heuristics (aimed at improving throughput) misfired under a sudden shift in request length distribution. The heuristic added an extra micro-delay while waiting for batches to fill; that delay interacted with our streaming flush path and produced the token gaps you observed.

Immediate fixes we’ve applied:
- Reverted the heuristic (permanent rollback).
- Added guardrails: a maximum batching window ceiling and a per-shard sequence-length monitor that prevents batching changes from triggering during rapid distribution shifts.
- Additional observability: added token-level latency dashboards and alerting for streaming token gaps.

Recommended long-term actions for NovusAI:
- If you run lots of variability in request lengths, set a soft-max_tokens guideline for heavy-concurrency endpoints.
- We’ll provide a short SDK patch that exposes a client-side hint to opt out of edge-level grouping for critical sessions.

Next steps:
- I can schedule a 30-minute technical postmortem with your infra team next week to walk through logs (Irene and Ben will join). Please share two 30-minute windows that work for you.
- We’ll send the formal PDF postmortem (attached) and a trimmed logs package for your SREs.

Attachments: postmortem-summary-20270312.pdf

If anything else emerges on your side, flag it in SUP-4581 and we’ll treat it as <priority>.

—Marissa
